title: Tambdi Jogeshwari
text:
Tambdi Jogeshwari (तांबडी जोगेश्वरी) — 2 (Dusra Manacha), located in Budhwar Peth, Pune, established 1893 (Ganeshotsav); Temple 15th century.

History: Tambdi Jogeshwari is primarily a temple of Goddess Jogeshwari, Pune's Gramdevi, distinct from Kasba Ganpati (Gramdevata); the Durga temple dates to the 15th century, one of Pune's oldest religious sites. Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations began here in 1893 when Bhau Bhendre introduced the idol, and Tilak gave it the second Manacha honour. Uniquely among the Manache 5, the idol is immersed and a new one installed every year. Since 2000 it has stood in a striking silver-dome pandal outside the temple, now an iconic Pune Ganeshotsav sight.

Idol/Deity: New idol installed every year — no permanent murti. Silver dome pandal (since 2000) is the visual centrepiece.

Temple/Mandir address: 33A, Budhwar Peth Road, Budhwar Peth, Pune 411002 (near Appa Balwant Chowk). Festival pandal address: TO UPDATE — silver dome outside the temple; confirm location for 2026. Maps link: TO UPDATE — check mandal's official pages in August 2026. Coordinates: 18.5175, 73.8562.

Aarti timings — Morning: Mangala Aarti: 6:00 AM; Evening: Sayan Aarti: 7:00 PM.

Special events during the 10 days: Eco-friendly themes in recent years; traditional fervour rituals; rich cultural programs.
